text:
Morgan: Quick RFC follow-up — thinking about shifting from weight-sum routing to explicit priority buckets with short preemptive windows. rough sketch below, want quick takes before i draft.

Priya: Curious — primary goal here is fairness under bursts or simplifying runtime?

Morgan: Both. weight-sum oscillates under bursty traffic. buckets let us give high-tier short guaranteed windows to reduce global thrash.

Dave: Windowing semantics? time-sliced or request-count sliced?

Morgan: Time-sliced. config idea:

```yaml
buckets:
  - name: platinum
    capacity_pct: 25
    preempt_window_ms: 200
    burst_tokens: 100
  - name: gold
    capacity_pct: 35
    preempt_window_ms: 100
    burst_tokens: 50
  - name: silver
    capacity_pct: 40
    preempt_window_ms: 0
    burst_tokens: 20
```

Morgan: semantics: during a platinum window (200ms every slot) platinum requests can preempt lower buckets at admission if burst_tokens permit. outside windows normal capacity_pct applies.

Priya: Starvation risk for silver during sustained platinum traffic?

Morgan: We'll add minimum guaranteed refill and anti-starvation multiplier when lower-tier latency exceeds threshold so silver still gets X tokens per Y ms.

Sam: Preemption implies evicting in-flight work or refusing admission. evicting is messy for KV/cache and streaming. how do we avoid dangerous cancels?

Morgan: Options: 1) only preempt at queue admission — simpler; 2) preempt in-progress but only for marked "preemptible" requests (embeddings, short jobs). in-progress preemptions need graceful cancel API.

Liz: Agree on marking. runtime should carry a preemptible flag. also we should avoid preempting streaming chat generations.

Priya: Telemetry: we must log preemption events with labels {victim_tier, preempter_tier, reason, request_id} and a metric counter + histogram for victim latency after preempt.

Morgan: Instrumentation plan: preempt_counter, preempt_latency_hist, trace spans linking request id to preemption event. hook into console alerts when preempt/sec > threshold.

Dave: Policy evaluation cost is a concern. global time-sliced buckets are cheap. per-tenant windows make eval heavier. do we want tenant overrides?

Morgan: Default = global buckets. tenant overrides enterprise-only. Dedicated tenants skip preemption entirely.

Sam: Could we implement as scoring: score = base + priority_boost(window_bonus)? scoring is cheap but gives soft guarantees only.

Morgan: Thinking hybrid: scoring for normal routing; hard-bucket fast-path when burst > capacity to enforce isolation.

Liz: Implementation detail: window schedule needs deterministic generator across nodes (monotonic clock + epoch seed) to avoid skew causing inconsistent admission decisions.

Priya: Control-plane failover: if policy store unreachable fall back to last-known-good config; if none, degrade to weight-sum with zero preempt windows.

Morgan: Agreed. product/billing question: if we preempt and reroute to cheaper model, how to bill? tag attempts and final served model in telemetry; finance/product to decide.

Priya: Also add an SLA signal: if preemptions cause lower-tier latency degradation, trigger automated mitigation (widen silver windows or throttle platinum).

Sam: For runtime complexity: prefer admission-only preempt first in beta. avoids cancel semantics and cache invalidation headaches.

Morgan: Next steps: i'll draft RFC including schema, runtime fast-path, lab chaos plan, telemetry dashboard mocks, and a migration checklist. will post here when ready. thanks!
